intended_object: The canonical morphism (in fact an isomorphism) (id_X)^* F → F, from the inverse image of a sheaf F on a space X along the identity map back to F. This comes from the docstring "canonical pullback transition along an identity map" and from how the file uses it as the unit case of the square-transition calculus.
explanation:
The body is `pullbackIdHom A Xi F`, defined in `PullbackCoherence.lean` as `(pullbackIdIso A X).hom.app F`. `pullbackIdIso` is `Adjunction.leftAdjointIdIso` applied to Mathlib's `TopCat.Sheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction A (𝟙 X)`, using the fact that pushforward along the identity is definitionally the identity functor. So the definition is the component at F of the canonical natural isomorphism id^* ≅ 𝟭, obtained from uniqueness of left adjoints. That is the standard canonical identification of id^* F with F.

The lemma `adjoint_identity` confirms the expected property: the adjoint of this map is 𝟙 F. Taken together, the definition and the lemma show it is the right canonical map, with the right direction.

The coefficient hypotheses on A (concrete category, limits and colimits, forgetful functor preserving limits and filtered colimits and reflecting isomorphisms) are exactly those Mathlib requires for `TopCat.Sheaf.pullback`. So the definition is not narrower than the setting in which sheaf pullback exists in Mathlib.

I found no Mathlib declaration for the identity-pullback isomorphism of sheaves on topological spaces, so there is no counterpart to cite. The definition is a thin wrapper, but the object it names is a genuine canonical morphism.
